  DRAFT MINUTES
  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
  JULY 28, 2025

  1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER
  A regular meeting of the Equestrian Committee of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was
  called to order by CHAIR SCHMITZ at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers of City Hall.

  2.  ROLL CALL
  Committee Members Present:  Griggs, Harik, Nilsen, Shinn, Silvano, Schmitz,
  Pope (arrived at 7:01 pm)
  Committee Members Absent:  Brtis, Martin, Romanelli
  City Staff Present:  Maintenance Superintendent Mike Goldsmith
  Community Services Supervisor Rosa Pinuelas

  3.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES
  A.  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES OF MARCH 24, 2025

  MEMBER SHINN moved, seconded by MEMBER HARIK to:

  APPROVE THE DRAFT MINUTES OF MARCH 24, 2025, EQUESTRIAN
  COMMITTEE MEETING
  There being no objection, CHAIR SCHMITZ so ordered.

  4.  AUDIENCE ITEMS WRITTEN/ORAL COMMUNICATIONS NOT ON AGENDA

  Audience Member Candy Young expressed concern regarding a Boy Scouts flag
  retirement ceremony involving a fire held in the City Hall parking lot near the
  Seahorse Riding Club (Seahorse). She expressed concern about the fire and
  stated that it posed a high risk to surrounding vegetation, nearby horses, and
  homes.
  MEMBER SILVANO expressed concern due to the proximity of the fire to pepper
  trees and Seahorse, the flammability of pepper trees, and the ability to evacuate
  horses in the event of a fire.
  MEMBER NILSEN also expressed concern about the activity, its proximity to
  Seahorse and the ability to evacuate horses in the event of a fire.
  MEMBER SHINN stated she also observed the fire, spoke with the Scouts on-site,
  and shared concerns regarding the activity. She stated that she hoped the activity

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES  1
July 28, 2025  3
   would not be allowed in the future and that future flag retirement ceremonies
  should be relocated outside the City.
  CHAIR SCHMITZ explained what a flag retirement ceremony entails, in response
  to MEMBER GRIGGS.
  CHAIR SCHMITZ noted that the Scouts have held flag retirement ceremonies in
  the past and that the Fire Department is aware and makes safety
  recommendations. She noted that it had been a couple years since the Scouts
  held a flag retirement ceremony in the City and that future considerations could be
  made. CHAIR SCHMITZ stated that the item is under staff review and would be
  carried forward to City Council for policy review.

  5.  STAFF ITEMS

  A.  PETER WEBER EQUESTRIAN CENTER RESTROOM PROJECT UPDATE
  (VERBAL REPORT)

  Supervisor Pinuelas provided a brief overview of the item.

  Supervisor Pinuelas reported that the project remains delayed due to coordination
  needed with multiple Los Angeles County and State Departments. She noted that
  due to the proximity to the landfill, additional regulatory compliance requirements
  must be met requiring review and approval from the multiple County and State
  departments. She reported that Supervisor Hahn’s office is assisting with efforts to
  get the project expedited. Supervisor Pinuelas also reported that portable restroom
  maintenance service is being reviewed with an additional day of servicing added,
  and that staff is looking to see if any other solutions are possible in the meantime.
  She shared that complaints had been received and that she or the Assistant City
  Manager, Alexa Davis could be contacted directly regarding complaints and
  concerns.

  B.  CITY CELEBRATION UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

  Supervisor Pinuelas provided a brief overview of the item.

  Supervisor Pinuelas provided an update on upcoming City Celebration planning.
  The event is scheduled for September 13, 2025 at the Empty Saddle Club with
  returning activities to include the magic show, equestrian events, petting zoo, pony
  rides, guided horse rides, corn pits, and rock-climbing wall. She stated that the DJ,
  and food vendors Smokeshow BBQ and Poppa Churro would also be returning.
  She reported that new elements being considered for this year’s event include an
  additional magic show, snow cones, and a photo booth. She noted that event
  sponsors are still being solicited and that the event had secured sponsorships from
  U.S. Bank and Waste Management each at the $1,000 level. Supervisor Pinuelas
  reported that the Palos Verdes Peninsula Horseman’s Association would be hosting

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES  2
July 28, 2025  4
   a raffle ride this year and that the equestrian drill team would again lead the flag
  salute.

  Discussion ensued regarding parking, potential sponsors, the raffle ride and prize
  donations.

  C.  MAYOR’S RIDE DEBRIEF (VERBAL REPORT)

  Supervisor Pinuelas provided a brief overview of the item.

  Supervisor Pinuelas reported that Mayor’s Ride was held on Saturday, May 10 with
  approximately 45–50 riders, including some members of the City Council and the
  Equestrian Committee, as well as local dignitaries, State Senator Ben Allen, and
  members of local equestrian groups. She stated that the ride concluded at Ernie
  Howlett Park with the Scouts’ Pancake Breakfast, which served about 675 meals.

  CHAIR SCHMITZ thanked the Committee for their efforts in getting the word out to
  the equestrian community and helping increase equestrian participation in the
  event.

  D.  EQUESTRIAN ISSUES LOG

  MEMBER HARIK thanked staff for trimming on the trail at George F Canyon.
  Superintendent Goldsmith responded, reporting on grading of the trail and that
  Maintenance staff would be constructing and installing a new bench at the top of
  the trail.

  Superintendent Goldsmith reported that sand was added to the Dapplegray Park
  round pen, dressage, and large arenas and that staff is currently working on the
  dressage arena at Ernie Howlett Park.

  Superintendent Goldsmith stated that hedge trimming is scheduled for the hedge
  located at the trail crossing of Ferncreek trail at Masongate, in response to
  MEMBER GRIGGS.

  E.  UPCOMING MEETING DATES (VERBAL REPORT)

  Supervisor Pinuelas provided a brief overview of the item.

  Supervisor Pinuelas noted the next meeting was scheduled for September 22,
  2025. She stated that the subsequent meeting was scheduled for November 24,
  2025, which falls during the week of the Thanksgiving holiday. She stated that staff
  recommended the Committee consider canceling the regular meeting scheduled
  for November 24 with the option to schedule a special meeting on November 17,
  2025.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES  3
July 28, 2025  5
   There was a consensus to move the November meeting date to Monday, November
  17, 2025.

  F.  MATTERS OF INTEREST (VERBAL REPORT)

  Supervisor Pinuelas reported that the Peter Weber Equestrian Center (PWEC)
  hayrides on the Palos Verdes Landfill have resumed. She noted the hours of
  operation had been posted on the City website, PWEC website, and shared via the
  City’s e-newsletter and by direct emails to the PWEC boarders.

  Discussion ensued regarding the importance of equestrian activities such as the
  PWEC hayrides and the recent Equine Emergency event, and how they support
  the City’s equestrian culture.

  Supervisor Pinuelas stated that she could provide a future update regarding halter
  and lead rope training for Sheriff’s deputies.

  6.  COMMITTEE REPORTS

  A.  ADOPT-A-TRAIL (VERBAL REPORT)

  Superintendent Goldsmith responded that staff would inspect the Ferncreek trail at
  Chalmette Lane for erosion near a recently installed pipe, in response to MEMBER
  GRIGGS.

  B.  MATTERS OF INTEREST (VERBAL REPORT)

  NONE.

  7.  ADJOURNMENT

  CHAIR SCHMITZ ADJOURNED THE MEETING AT 7:36 p.m.

  Respectfully submitted,  Approved,

  MATT MORROW, COMMUNITY SERVICE COORDINATOR

SUBJECT: 2025 CITY CELEBRATION DEBRIEF
______________________________________________________________________

OVERVIEW

The 68th Annual City Celebration was held on September 13, 2025, at Ernie Howlett Park.
Staff is bringing forward comments and suggestions received from the City Celebration
Subcommittee, Parks and Activities Commission, Staff, and event participants for the
Equestrian Committee’s review.

BACKGROUND

The City Celebration was held at Ernie Howlett Park on the sports fields on Saturday,
September 13, 2025, from 9:00 am to 3:00 pm. The following comments and suggestions were
collected by Staff to consider for the planning of next year’s 69th Annual City Celebration event:

Venue

  1. Ernie Howlett Park was utilized as the venue for this year’s City Celebration. On
  September 4, 2025, Staff in consultation with the City Celebration Subcommittee
  decided to move the event to Ernie Howlett Park as a precautionary measure and in
  response to concerns from the local equestrian community about reported cases of
  Equine Strangles illness.

  2. Out of an abundance of caution for the public and equestrian community due to the
  equestrian illness, animal-related event activities (pony rides, petting zoo, and guided
  horse rides) were cancelled this year. Due to the quick location change, the hayride was
  also cancelled. With these activities being cancelled and the ample space available on
  the sports fields at Ernie Howlett Park, Staff was able to secure four large inflatable
  activities (80’ obstacle course w/slide, Toddler Corn Maze Obstacle Course, 4-Sport
  Challenge Games, and an Inflatable Pony Race) for the event. Face painting, the rock-
  climbing wall, and the free magic show were still offered as activities and entertainment.
  A digital photo booth was newly added to this year’s event.

  3. DJ Aaron, owner of Night to Remember DJs, again provided music, sound, and emcee
  services, along with the digital photo booth for event attendees.

Equestrian Committee Staff Report – February 9, 2026  City of Rolling Hills Estates –  1
2025 City Celebration Debrief  7
   4. Two 15’ x 25’ canopies were again rented for the picnic table area to provide a shaded
  eating area. An extra 15’ x 25’ canopy was rented to provide a shaded area for the face
  painting activity due to the sports fields not having any natural shade available.

  5. Extra portable restrooms and hand-washing stations were rented to address the lack of
  nearby restroom facilities, as the event was held on the sports fields.

  6. Parking for event attendees was more available and easier to manage due to the ample
  parking at Ernie Howlett Park.

General Event Details

  1.  Due to the last-minute event changes and the lack of infrastructure on the sports
  fields to support the City’s electronic payment system, it was determined that it would
  be best to provide all event activities at no cost this year. Thus, all activities and
  entertainment were available without tickets or wristbands, unlike in previous years.

  2.  The event was well attended considering the last-minute location change and the
  cancellation of equestrian-related activities, which occurred ten days prior to the
  event. Staff estimated nearly 1,000 attendees between 11:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m., the
  event’s peak period. It has been suggested that offering the activities for free may
  have contributed to both the attendance numbers and to the attendees staying
  longer at the event.

  3.  Due to the cancellation of equestrian-related activities, the Palos Verdes Junior Drill
  Team was unable to lead this year’s flag salute. Staff was able to secure Scout
  Troop #258 who led the flag salute prior to the Mayor’s remarks.

  4.  The Mayor’s Welcome was held in a centralized location of the event area on the
  sports fields incorporating the use of the DJ’s sound system for the speech.

  5.  One cake and 240 cupcakes were purchased again this year. This amount worked
  well, and both continue to be popular options with most preferring cupcakes.

  6.  Lunch service was once again provided by Smoke Show BBQ and appeared to be
  very well received again this year. They offered three BBQ entrée options with a
  side of coleslaw and chips. These options included a pastrami sandwich, a pulled
  pork sandwich, or a smashburger for $15. They also offered a hot dog and chips
  combo for $5. They sold waters and sodas this year as Empty Saddle normally
  provides beverage services for this event. We have not received information yet
  from the vendor regarding total sales, but they were very satisfied with the turnout
  and have requested to return next year. They were again able to take credit card
  payments, which worked well and helped to keep the line moving. The lunch service
  was available from 11:00 am – 2:00 pm.

  7.  Popa Churro also returned this year and sold freshly made churros and deep-fried
  Oreos throughout the event from 9:00 am to 3:00 pm. We have not received

   information from the vendor regarding sales, but they were also very satisfied with
  the turnout and have requested to return for next year’s event.

  8.  A new food vendor at this year’s event was Kona Ice. They provided a truck that
  served shaved ice with different syrup options throughout the event from 9:00 am to
  3:00 pm. We have not yet received information from the vendor regarding total sales,
  but they were also very satisfied with the turnout and have requested to return for
  next year’s event.

  9.  The USC football team had an away game at Purdue on our 2025 event date and
  the UCLA football team had a home game that was played on the night prior to our
  2025 event date. The finalized Big 10 Conference Football schedule is usually
  available by May each year; however, looking forward to potential City Celebration
  2026 dates, no games have been scheduled. Staff will continue to monitor the
  schedule.

Below are upcoming Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur holidays which are considered when
planning the event each year. The 2026 Rosh Hashanah holiday coincides with one of the
potential 2026 City Celebration dates:

  Rosh Hashanah Dates  Yom Kippur  Proposed
Year  Begins at Sundown Ends at Nightfall  Dates  City Celebration Date(s)

2026  Fri., Sept. 11  Sun., Sept. 13  Sept. 20-21  Sat., Sept. 19 (avoids Sept. 12)
2027  Fri., Oct. 1  Sun., Oct. 3  Oct. 10-11  Sat., Sept. 11 (or 18)

Other event dates to take into consideration when planning for the 2026 City Celebration are
the Portuguese Bend Horse Show, which is confirmed to be held September 4, 5, and 6 in
2026. The Beachlife Ranch Music Festival has been indefinitely suspended and is not planned
to be scheduled in 2026. The Empty Saddle Club also holds their annual Cowboy Days event
annually, but in 2025 it was held in June. Previously when scheduled in September they
coordinated a date that is generally after the City Celebration.

Proposed date for the 2026 City Celebration is Saturday, September 19, 2026.

Volunteers and Vendor Booths

  1. There were 40 youth volunteers throughout the event from five youth agencies
  (Assisteens, PV Assembly, Lion’s Heart, National League of Young Men, and Girl
  Scouts). Volunteers helped with morning set up, children’s activities, cake/cupcake
  distribution and afternoon clean up.

  2. EMT services were again provided by Event Med Staff with one EMT staff on standby
  during the entire event for a cost of $300. There were no incidents requiring EMT
  response.

  3. Five community organizations hosted information booths this year, the same number
  hosted in 2024.
Equestrian Committee Staff Report – February 9, 2026  City of Rolling Hills Estates –  3
2025 City Celebration Debrief
  9
   4. Two sponsors hosted booths this year. Commercial booth spaces were not offered this
  year due to limited space at Empty Saddle Club, and the Subcommittee determined
  that the allocation of booth space should be prioritized for sponsors and local community
  non-profit organizations. However, commercial entities still had the option to sponsor
  the event at the $500 level to become eligible for booth space.

Entertainment and Activities

  1. Horsemanship events were cancelled this year out of an abundance of caution due to
  the reported cases of Equine Strangles.

  2. The PVP Horsemen’s Association also postponed the Annual Poker Ride due to the
  horse disease, the date is yet to be determined.

  3. The popular stick horse rodeo was held in front of the stage from 11:30 am to noon this
  year, which worked well.

  4. A free magic show was held again this year and was well received. It took place
  following the Mayor’s remarks from 1:30 – 2:00 p.m. on the stage.

  5. Staff, with the assistance of volunteers, coordinated the watermelon eating contest as
  the final activity of the event, which was popular once again this year.

  6. All activities were offered throughout the event from 9:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. again this
  year. Due to changes to the event this year, all activities were free, and no tickets or
  wristbands were sold. The petting zoo, pony rides, and guided horse rides were
  cancelled out of an abundance of caution for the animals. Face painting and the rock-
  climbing wall remained very popular.

  7. Face painting continues to be a highly popular activity. Staff secured a different vendor
  this year who provided three face painters throughout the event, which improved
  operational efficiency.

  8. Residents received an informational postcard with two “Gold” postcard tickets in the
  mail allowing admission to one activity per “ticket” again this year. These tickets were
  not utilized this year, but the mailer still remains an excellent marketing tool for the event.

  9. Two corn pits were available again this year – one for ages 4 and under, and one for
  ages 5-9. They were offered as a free activity and remained very popular.

  10. The hayride was cancelled this year due to the location change and insufficient time to
  plan the logistics. Instead, the wagon was positioned in an area that provided attendees
  with a popular photo opportunity at the event.

  11. Prior to the location change, adjustments were planned for the number of tickets
  required for certain activities at this year’s event. While ticket pricing remained the
  same, the price of the all-day wristband was planned to increase by $5.

  12. Two wooden horses, constructed by the City’s Maintenance Division, along with two
  wooden horses borrowed from the Los Alamitos Historic Ranch and Gardens, were
  available again this year and attracted families whose children sat in the saddles for fun
  and photos. The photo area was enhanced this year with the hay wagon, hay bales,
  and the wooden horses.

  13. Lowes again donated craft kits which were distributed as prizes for games again this
  year.

  14. Staff recommends continuing to have all activities available during the entire time of the
  event (from 9:00 am to 3:00 pm) as it continues to be very successful.

Promotions

1.  A direct mailer was sent out in the form of a flyer (folded in half) that included (2) free
  passes to the ticketed activities. The mailer was sent to every residence and proved to
  be effective again. The mailer was printed using a vendor and sent out using a mail
  service which continues to be cost-effective in comparison to past costs. Any residents
  who do not receive the mailers are invited to stop by City Hall and are given mailers.
  Total cost of the mailer was $2,015.86 this year compared to $1,993.76 in 2024.

2.  A variety of other promotions assisted in drawing event attendees, including the use of
  Eventbrite announcements and the continued use of the Community Services
Equestrian Committee Staff Report – February 9, 2026  City of Rolling Hills Estates –  5
2025 City Celebration Debrief
  11
   Department’s enhanced flyer graphics, the City’s special events webpage, banners for
  the City Celebration placed in the City’s rights-of-way, flyers placed at City facilities,
  press releases, PVP Horsemen’s Association Dispatch Newsletter, PV Patch event
  announcements, PVPUSD on-line newsletter, City social media postings and paid
  advertisements.

Consideration For Next Year

At the City Celebration Subcommittee debrief meeting on November 5, 2025, the
Subcommittee discussed venue options for future City Celebration events. The Subcommittee
expressed interest in alternating the event location between Ernie Howlett Park and the Empty
Saddle Club in future years; however, it recommends returning the event to Ernie Howlett Park
in 2026, including reinstating equestrian events, like Gymkhana, pony rides and the Poker
Ride, if feasible, and charging for select activities. This report will also be presented to the
Equestrian Committee. Input is appreciated for consideration of the 2026 event; however,
confirmation will be determined as preliminary planning for next year’s event moves forward.

Financial Summary

  1. Sponsorship totaled $3,000 and included Waste Management ($1,000), US Bank
  ($1,000), Fusion Academy Palos Verdes ($500), and Peninsula Heritage School
  ($500), compared to a total of $3,000 in 2024. In-kind donations were received from
  Bennett Landscaping (straw for hay bales and flowers for tables), Leach Grain & Milling
  Co. (50% seed corn discount), Lomita Feed Store (hay bales), and Lowe’s (children’s
  craft activity kits given out as prizes).

  2. A negative revenue vs. expenses balance of approximately ($15,370.68) was realized
  this year, compared to a negative balance of ($7,451.55) in 2024. This increase is
  attributed to the absence of revenue from ticket and wristband sales, the cancellation
  of equestrian events (Gymkhana), and the postponement of the Poker Ride.

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommends that the Equestrian Committee receive and file this report. This staff report
will also be shared with the City Council as an informational item.
